Monad::join.obligation: Invoke the implementation-supplied bind with identity callback, moving the inner wrapped value. This derived operation is only as lawful/total as the supplied Monad; no generic monad law admission occurs.

checked_clone.signature: fn checked_clone<T: Clone + Eq>( value: &T, law: AlgebraLaw, index: usize, ) -> Result<T, LawCheckError>
checked_clone.body: { let copy = value.clone(); if copy != *value { return Err(LawCheckError::NonPreservingClone { law, index }); } Ok(copy) }
checked_clone.obligation: Clone exactly once, compare that copy to the original under supplied Eq and refuse NonPreservingClone with the exact law/index before callback evaluation. Return that same checked copy; no second unverified clone. Eq/Clone semantics, side effects, panic/drop and allocation remain caller contracts.

Phantom::new.obligation: Construct only PhantomData; no carrier value, action, evidence or mathematical object is manufactured.

EMAlgebra::verify_laws.signature: pub fn verify_laws(&self) -> bool where A: Clone + Eq, M::T<A>: Clone + Eq, M::T<M::T<A>>: Clone,
EMAlgebra::verify_laws.obligation: Deprecated no-domain compatibility method always returns false (unverified), even for lawful actions. It invokes no callback and does not emit a counterexample or universal certificate.

EMAlgebra::check_samples.signature: pub fn check_samples( &self, unit_samples: Vec<A>, associativity_samples: Vec<M::T<M::T<A>>>, ) -> Result<AlgebraSampleCheck, LawCheckError> where A: Eq, M::T<M::T<A>>: Eq,
EMAlgebra::check_samples.body: { let observed = AlgebraSampleCheck { unit_samples: unit_samples.len(), associativity_samples: associativity_samples.len(), }; for (index, value) in unit_samples.into_iter().enumerate() { let copy = checked_clone(&value, AlgebraLaw::Unit, index)?; if (self.action)(M::unit::<A>(copy)) != value { return Err(LawCheckError::Violated { law: AlgebraLaw::Unit, index, }); } } for (index, value) in associativity_samples.into_iter().enumerate() { let copy = checked_clone(&value, AlgebraLaw::Associativity, index)?; let left = (self.action)(M::fmap::<M::T<A>, A>(|ta| (self.action)(ta), copy)); let right = (self.action)(M::join::<A>(value)); if left != right { return Err(LawCheckError::Violated { law: AlgebraLaw::Associativity, index, }); } } Ok(observed) }
EMAlgebra::check_samples.obligation: Capture both Vec lengths, scan owned unit samples then associativity samples in input order with phase-local usize enumerate indices. Each input is shared by one checked Clone. Unit compares h(unit(copy)) with original; associativity compares h(fmap(h,copy)) with h(join(original)), moving fmap inner values without redundant clones. First clone/law refusal returns exact phase/index and prevents later evaluation. Success reports supplied lengths only, including vacuous empty lists.

AlgebraMorphism::respects_algebras.signature: pub fn respects_algebras(&self, _dom: &EMAlgebra<M, A>, _cod: &EMAlgebra<M, B>) -> bool where A: Clone, B: Clone + Eq, M::T<A>: Clone, M::T<B>: Clone,
AlgebraMorphism::respects_algebras.obligation: Deprecated no-domain compatibility query always returns false/unverified. It neither evaluates candidates nor establishes invalidity; use supplied finite observations instead.

AlgebraMorphism::check_samples.signature: pub fn check_samples( &self, dom: &EMAlgebra<M, A>, cod: &EMAlgebra<M, B>, samples: Vec<M::T<A>>, ) -> Result<usize, LawCheckError> where B: Eq, M::T<A>: Eq,
AlgebraMorphism::check_samples.body: { let count = samples.len(); for (index, value) in samples.into_iter().enumerate() { let copy = checked_clone(&value, AlgebraLaw::Morphism, index)?; let left = (self.f)((dom.action)(copy)); let right = (cod.action)(M::fmap::<A, B>(&self.f, value)); if left != right { return Err(LawCheckError::Violated { law: AlgebraLaw::Morphism, index, }); } } Ok(count) }
AlgebraMorphism::check_samples.obligation: Scan owned wrapped inputs once, cloning and checking each shared input before callbacks. Compare f(dom.action(copy)) with cod.action(fmap(f,original)); first refusal returns Morphism and exact index. Success returns input Vec length, not universal preservation or endpoint admission.

FreeAlgebraFunctor::map.body: { EMAlgebra { carrier: Phantom::new(), action: Box::new(|tta: M::T<M::T<A>>| M::join(tta)), } }

MaybeMonad::bind.signature: fn bind<A: Obj, B: Obj>(ta: Maybe<A>, f: impl Fn(A) -> Maybe<B>) -> Maybe<B>
MaybeMonad::bind.body: { match ta { Maybe::Just(x) => f(x), Maybe::Nothing => Maybe::Nothing, } }
MaybeMonad::bind.obligation: Nothing returns Nothing without invoking f; Just(x) invokes the supplied f once and returns its exact wrapped result. Callback behavior is external; concrete pure value equations match Option.bind.

MaybeMonad::fmap.obligation: Delegate to this actual bind, applying f once only to Just and rewrapping with unit. No input cloning, coercion, hidden numerical operation or None callback.
